clue.text: Old academic institution beginning to plan for growth

parts.note: a POLY was a British polytechnic, a type of college merged into the universities in 1992

indicators.note: the beginning of the word plan is its opening letter, which is all we take

explanation.surface: A former polytechnic draws up the first stage of its expansion plans.
explanation.walkthrough: 'growth' looks like part of the college's plan, but it is the definition: a polyp is a small growth on body tissue.
explanation.definitionFit: A polyp is a small abnormal lump of tissue, a medical kind of growth.

clue.text: Novel suggestion for increasing queen's welcome?

definitions.meaning: a 1942 Evelyn Waugh novel about wartime England
a jokey proposal to hang out extra bunting when a queen visits

explanation.surface: A novel idea for giving a visiting queen a bigger reception.
explanation.definitionFit: Waugh's comic war novel has that title, and the phrase literally urges displaying more bunting for a royal visit.

clue.text: Instruments as others but less loud

indicators.note: less means the letter for loud is subtracted

parts.note: flutes are other musical instruments
F is forte, the musical direction for loud

explanation.surface: Some instruments are like the others but quieter.
explanation.definitionFit: Lutes are plucked stringed instruments with a rounded back.

clue.text: Body-builder favouring loaf to get inner energy

parts.note: pro means in favour of

indicators.note: to get inner tells us the energy letter goes inside the loaf

parts.note: a tin is a loaf baked in a rectangular tin
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: A bodybuilder prefers bread to boost his energy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Body-builder' suggests a gym-goer; protein is what builds body tissue. A TIN is a British loaf baked in a tin.
explanation.definitionFit: Protein is the nutrient that builds and repairs muscle and tissue.

clue.text: One advertising starters for inn's customers within bar menu

indicators.note: within tells us the first letters go inside the other piece

parts.note: a menu in a bar could be called a pub list

indicators.note: the starters for the words inn's and customers are their opening letters

explanation.surface: A promoter chooses the starters on a pub menu to tempt an inn's customers.
explanation.definitionFit: A publicist's job is to promote clients, so the role is a kind of advertiser.

clue.text: Anaemic-sounding water-carrier

indicators.note: sounding means the word for anaemic is heard, not spelt

parts.note: an anaemic person looks pale

explanation.surface: A water bucket that looks rather washed out.
explanation.definitionFit: A pail is a bucket for carrying water.

clue.text: Tight-lipped and presumably lacking zip!

definitions.meaning: a garment fastened with buttons rather than a zip fastener

explanation.surface: Someone reserved and, by the sound of it, lacking energy.
explanation.definitionFit: Being reserved and silent is an idiom for being fastened shut, and a shirt done up with buttons needs no zip.

clue.text: One circling Saturn needs momentum: this initially lost, a replacement needed

indicators.note: this refers back to momentum, and its initial letter is lost from the synonym
replacement needed means another letter fills the gap left by the lost one

parts.note: impetus is the force or momentum of a moving body
taken as written, the letter that goes in

explanation.surface: Instructions for keeping a satellite moving around Saturn after it loses speed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'this initially' refers back to 'momentum', so its initial M is removed from IMPETUS and replaced by A.
explanation.definitionFit: Iapetus is one of the large moons orbiting Saturn.

clue.text: Possibly noticing nothing as disguised person appears?

indicators.note: possibly says the letters of noticing could be arranged another way

parts.note: O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: Perhaps nobody notices a person in disguise turning up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Possibly' rearranges NOTICING to give INCOGNIT, and O for 'nothing' finishes it.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone travelling incognito conceals their identity, just as a person in disguise shows up.

clue.text: Scruffy kids excited by old master in Tate

indicators.note: excited suggests the letters of old master in Tate are stirred up into a new order

explanation.surface: Grubby children get thrilled by an Old Master painting at the Tate gallery.
explanation.walkthrough: The Tate is a group of London art galleries.
explanation.definitionFit: A tatterdemalion is a person in ragged clothes, a ragamuffin.

clue.text: Is head of theatre backing Edinburgh's show designer?

indicators.note: backing here means following on behind, so these pieces come after the show

parts.note: the Edinburgh Military Tattoo is a famous annual display of military bands

indicators.note: the head of the word theatre is its opening letter

explanation.surface: A question about whether a theatre director is supporting a famous Edinburgh show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'show designer' reads as one job, but 'show' belongs to the Edinburgh Tattoo; 'designer' alone defines someone who creates tattoos.
explanation.definitionFit: A tattooist creates designs on skin, so the trade is that of a body-art designer.

clue.text: Lacy decoration gives bed very good edging

indicators.note: edging means sitting at the edge, so this piece goes at the front of the bed

parts.note: PI, short for pious, is crossword shorthand for very good in a saintly sense
a cot is a small bed

explanation.surface: Fancy lace trim adds a lovely border to a bed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'edging' looks like part of the lace definition, but it only places PI ahead of COT.
explanation.definitionFit: A picot is a small loop of thread forming an ornamental edge on lace or ribbon.

clue.text: Coat of gloss with edges cut in

indicators.note: cut in means the other outer letter is also moved into the body of the word
the edges of the word for gloss are its first and last letters, and the first of these shifts inward

parts.note: lustre is a shine or gloss on a surface

explanation.surface: Instructions for a coat of gloss paint, carefully cutting in at the edges.
explanation.walkthrough: 'edges cut in' moves both outer letters of LUSTRE inwards: L goes after U, and E goes before R. 'Coat of gloss' sounds like painting, but 'Coat' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: An ulster is a long, loose overcoat, originally made in Belfast.

clue.text: Bard's house producing visual display for all to see inside

indicators.note: inside tells us the second piece goes into the first

parts.note: a montage is a composite picture or sequence of images
U is the British film classification meaning suitable for everyone

explanation.surface: A theatre stages an exhibition everyone can view.
explanation.walkthrough: The Bard is Shakespeare; the Montagues are Romeo's family, the house rivalling the Capulets in Romeo and Juliet.
explanation.definitionFit: In Shakespeare's Romeo and Juliet the Montague family is one of the two feuding noble houses of Verona.

clue.text: Vegetable with banger isn't cooked

indicators.note: cooked suggests the letters of banger isn't are reworked into a new order

explanation.surface: A vegetable is served with a sausage that hasn't been cooked.
explanation.walkthrough: A BANGER is British slang for a sausage.
explanation.definitionFit: String beans are green bean pods eaten as a vegetable.

clue.text: Salesgirl has sort of dress material the husband's not wanted

parts.note: a midi is a dress reaching to mid-calf
net is a mesh fabric

indicators.note: not wanted tells us the letter for husband is removed from the word the

parts.note: H is a standard abbreviation for husband

explanation.surface: A shop assistant is selling dress fabric that her husband dislikes.
explanation.walkthrough: Deleting H from THE leaves TE.
explanation.definitionFit: A midinette is a Parisian shop assistant or seamstress, especially in a fashion house.

clue.text: Something unsuccessful set up by a guy?

definitions.meaning: an anticlimax or let-down that fails to impress
a firework set off beside a guy, the effigy burnt on Bonfire Night

explanation.surface: A failure arranged by some man.
explanation.walkthrough: On Guy Fawkes Night, 5 November, Britons burn an effigy called a guy and let off fireworks such as squibs.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom for a disappointing flop, from a firecracker that fizzles out because it got wet.

clue.text: Was agent full of zest caught out?

indicators.note: out means the letter for caught is left out

parts.note: spiced means flavoured with lively, zesty seasoning
C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: A question about whether a lively spy was found out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'agent' suggests a spy being caught; in fact 'Was agent' is the past-tense definition and 'caught' only supplies C.
explanation.definitionFit: To act as an agent in espionage is to keep watch secretly, and the past tense describes having done so.

clue.text: Business course giving priority to sport and dance

indicators.note: the business course gives priority to the sport, so the sport is placed first

parts.note: RU stands for rugby union
an MBA is a Master of Business Administration degree

explanation.surface: A business course puts sport and dancing ahead of study.
explanation.definitionFit: The rumba is a Cuban ballroom dance in a lively rhythm.

clue.text: Frail men tend to catch this illness

indicators.note: to catch means the letters run across the words frail men tend and are caught within them

explanation.surface: Weak men are prone to picking up this disease.
explanation.definitionFit: An ailment is a minor illness or disorder.

clue.text: Such could be one sister, I conceive

definitions.text: Such could be one sister, I conceive

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I
a sister in a religious order is a nun
to conceive an idea is to form it

explanation.surface: Someone muses that a nun is the sort of person who fits the description.
explanation.walkthrough: A nun wears a habit and so is dressed in uniform, which the whole clue hints at.
explanation.definitionFit: Members of religious orders wear a habit, so a nun is someone dressed in official costume.

clue.text: I am on lake running over head of stupid duck

indicators.note: in a down clue on means placed above, so the contraction comes first

parts.note: I'm is the contraction of I am

indicators.note: running over means the lake runs right over and around the following letter, enclosing it

parts.note: a mere is a lake

indicators.note: the head of the word stupid is its opening letter

explanation.surface: Someone at a lake runs over a silly duck's head.
explanation.walkthrough: 'duck' looks like the bird, but it is the verb meaning to plunge under water. 'running over' puts S inside MERE.
explanation.definitionFit: To duck someone is to push them under water, which is to submerge them.

clue.text: Long body of female to exploit beer? Not right!

parts.note: to use something is to exploit it

indicators.note: Not tells us the letter for right is taken out of the beer

parts.note: lager is a type of beer

explanation.surface: A complaint that a woman is wrong to take advantage of beer.
explanation.walkthrough: Removing R from LAGER leaves LAGE.
explanation.definitionFit: The fuselage is the main elongated hull of an aircraft.

clue.text: Are millions said to be lacking principles?

parts.note: an are is a metric unit of area, abbreviated A
M is the abbreviation for million
oral means spoken rather than written

explanation.surface: A question about whether millionaires are thought to be unscrupulous.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Are' looks like a verb, but it is the hundred-square-metre unit of area.
explanation.definitionFit: Amoral describes someone with no moral sense at all, without ethical standards.

clue.text: Part of big firm ripping off British farm

indicators.note: ripping off means the letter for British is torn away

parts.note: a branch is a local office of a large company

explanation.surface: A division of a large company is cheating a British farm.
explanation.definitionFit: A ranch is a large farm, especially for raising livestock.

clue.text: Primate embracing saint? That could be a feature of the church

indicators.note: embracing means the primate holds the saint's letter inside

parts.note: an ape is a primate

explanation.surface: An ape hugging a holy figure, as might be carved in a church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Primate' could be an archbishop, which suits the church setting, but here it is the animal.
explanation.definitionFit: An apse is the semicircular recess at the east end of a church.

clue.text: A darling quick on the uptake

parts.note: something darling is sweet or cute

explanation.surface: Someone sweet who is also sharp-witted.
explanation.definitionFit: An acute mind is sharp and perceptive, quick to understand.

clue.text: English prose tricky for worker to get into? This is trickier!

indicators.note: to get into means the worker goes inside the scrambled letters
tricky suggests the letters of prose are twisted into an awkward new order

parts.note: an ant is the classic crossword worker, from the worker ant

explanation.surface: Someone finds English prose difficult for a labourer to master, then says a different language is harder still.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tricky' rearranges PROSE into SPERO, which ANT enters. The definition jokes that an invented language is even harder to get into than English prose.
explanation.definitionFit: Esperanto is an invented international language, here offered as something harder to learn than English writing.

clue.text: Subject matter? Junior editor has opinion

parts.note: a sub, or sub-editor, is a junior newspaper editor
a stance is a position or opinion on an issue

explanation.surface: A newspaper's sub-editor has a view on what the article covers.
explanation.definitionFit: The substance of a piece is its essential content or topic.

clue.text: Old character's very big motivating force

parts.note: eth is an old letter of Old English and Icelandic
OS stands for outsize, a very large clothing size

explanation.surface: Someone's ancient character is a huge driving influence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'character' suggests personality, but it is a letter of an old alphabet.
explanation.definitionFit: An ethos is the guiding spirit or set of beliefs that drives a group or person.
